source_review.notes: Reviewed the Bernstein-Hadzilacos-Goodman text; Coffman-Elphick-Shoshani DOI/bibliographic record; primary Chandy-Misra-Haas paper; current PostgreSQL 18 deadlock and deadlock_timeout documentation; MySQL 8.4 deadlock, detector, and error-scope documentation; and current SQL Server 17 deadlock/system_health documentation. All ten cited destinations were retrieved and retained locally or represented by primary paper plus authoritative DOI metadata. Product behavior is version/configuration scoped, including detector cadence, victim heuristics, graph limits, rollback scope, and evidence capture.

evidence: Checked W=(V,E), waiter-to-blocker edge direction, owner/request/block predicates, SCC/self-loop, victim, cost, blocking, deadlock, starvation, livelock, prevention, avoidance, and signature definitions.
Checked wait-for graph is consistently distinguished from precedence/serialization graph.
Checked cycle statements are explicitly scoped to exact current conjunctive single-site grant dependencies.
Checked transaction, task, session, prepared participant, resource, conversion, and queue identities are not conflated.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Detection, victim policy, recovery, retry, fairness, observability, and prevention are modeled as separate responsibilities.

evidence: Independently enumerated reachability rather than importing the chapter's Tarjan implementation.
Recomputed cycle members as T1,T2,T3 and collateral waiter as T4.
Recomputed victim scores T1=(0,4300,800), T2=(1,700,200), and T3=(0,1300,500), selecting T3.
After independently removing T3 incident edges, recomputed remaining edges T1->T2 and T4->T2 with no cycle and independent_invariants=True.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The independent calculation is retained at artifacts/reviews/DBE-045/independent-recomputation.txt.

evidence: Re-derived cycle sufficiency by assuming a first progressor and following its required predecessor around the cycle to contradiction.
Re-derived cycle necessity for a finite deadlocked set by repeatedly following one required internal blocker until a vertex repeats.
Re-derived that removing every incident edge of a selected vertex breaks each simple cycle containing that vertex but may leave other cycles, requiring re-detection.
Constructed stale-distributed-snapshot, OR-wait, and multiple-instance countermodels showing why the simple theorem cannot be exported unchanged.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proof assumes exact simultaneous edges, conjunctive pending requests, no alternative instance/progress path, and actionable abort scope.

evidence: Reviewed acyclic chains, two/three-way cycles, self-loop, conversion, multiple blockers, queue bypass, collateral waiters, overlapping cycles, and complex SCCs.
Reviewed stale snapshots, OR waits, multiple instances, distributed probes, local detector blind spots, application mutex/pool cycles, parallel workers, and prepared transactions.
Reviewed cheapest/youngest/oldest/largest-release victim policies, priority spoofing, ties, ineligible work, repeated victimization, starvation, and rollback cost uncertainty.

Reviewed doom/interrupt/undo/release/wake ordering, statement versus transaction rollback, pool reset, external effects, retry budgets, jitter, deadlines, livelock, overload, failover, and evidence privacy.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Every mitigation preserves the business invariant and recovery boundary before optimizing wait counts or rollback cost.

evidence: The repository verifier matched exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status for the SCC/victim model.
The model checks exact cycle component, excludes T4 collateral, selects T3 by the documented score, removes all victim edges, and verifies acyclicity.

Manual review checked exact edge derivation, identity mapping, eligible deterministic victim choice, doom before new work, undo before exposure, complete cleanup, grant re-evaluation, full-transaction retry, and bounded retry admission.
Draft validation accepted exact front matter, required sections, ten examples, five exercises/answers, local links, citations, and executable evidence before stopping only for review evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: The model is an immutable finite graph and omits live lock queues, concurrency, rollback, distributed messages, multiple resource instances, engine integrations, and workload performance.

evidence: Reviewed cycle necessity and sufficiency assumptions and both proof directions line by line.
Reviewed SCC criteria, including singleton self-loop and the fact that one victim may not clear every cycle in an SCC.
Reviewed resolution argument from victim doom through protected undo, edge removal, waiter wake/recheck, and repeated detection.
Reviewed all exercise answers for exact edge construction, countermodels, independent oracles, victim/fairness policy, and cross-engine incident diagnosis.
proof_review.notes: No proof of vendor detector completeness, distributed observation consistency, victim optimality, starvation freedom, rollback implementation, or retry convergence is claimed.

evidence: The cycle argument is explicitly labeled with its conjunctive single-site model and assumptions.
The executable victim score is explicitly identified as a teaching policy rather than vendor behavior.
Timeout, monitoring snapshot, current product behavior, and distributed detection claims are carefully separated from formal cycle proof.
Audited detects, proves, deadlocked, sufficient, necessary, safe, atomic, complete, current, always, prevents, and optimal language for scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current implementation examples are evidence of documented behavior, not universal semantics or formal verification of the products.

evidence: The standard-library SCC and victim model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
A separate reachability enumeration independently reproduced membership, collateral classification, score, victim, and post-removal acyclicity.
All ten references were retrieved and checked for the cited foundational or current behavior.
Production claims require native graph, version/configuration, transaction, plan, resource/mode, victim, rollback, retry, latency, commit, and invariant evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live database deadlock, conversion, range/metadata lock, worker/exchange dependency, victim rollback, external effect, distributed detector, failover, or contention benchmark was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives deadlock from exact wait dependencies and distinguishes detection from ordinary blocking, timeout, victim policy, recovery, starvation, prevention, and distributed observation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed queue/conversion edges, detector frequency, eligibility/cost/fairness, rollback-safe cleanup, full-transaction idempotent retry, cross-layer blind spots, normalized signatures, and current PostgreSQL/InnoDB/SQL Server evidence.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, scoped theorem, executable SCC/victim trace, ten distinct examples, and five exercises progress from graph retrieval through proof, implementation testing, policy design, and cross-engine production transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter does not certify a vendor detector, graph completeness, victim optimality, rollback implementation, distributed dependency model, retry safety for a specific application, workload, or production configuration.
